title: Hearthlight: Cozy Farming Sound Effects
shortText: 107 cozy farming SFX: 8 crops, each plant, water, grow, ripe and harvest, plus tools, kitchen and home. WAV + OGG.
html:
Every crop from the seed to the basket

107 cozy farming sound effects: 8 crops, and every one ships the same 5 stage chain, from planting to the harvest coming off, each crop harvested its own way.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 27 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The turnip and the apple tree complete, every stage and every take, the first harvest of the other 6 crops, the hearth and night loops, the harvest basket filling, a hoe stroke, an axe chop and two interface ticks.

One chain, every crop

A farming game repeats one loop all day: plant, water, wait, harvest. Every crop here ships that loop under the same names:

  • plant: fingers in the soil and the seed set down
  • water: a pour over the plant, leaves pattering and soil soaking
  • grow: the plant filling out between days, longer for bigger plants
  • ripe: a soft sparkle, it is ready
  • harvest: two takes, the crop coming off its own way

So you wire a crop once and only its name changes: turnip_water, pumpkin_water, apple_water. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: all 8 crops carry exactly this chain, and the 80 pairs of stages inside each crop all differ.

The crops and how they come off

  • Turnip: a root crop you pull, soil tearing as it comes up.
  • Lettuce: a leafy head that snaps off crisp at the base.
  • Strawberry: a low berry plant, small soft pops as you pick.
  • Corn: a tall stalk, the cob cracking off its husk.
  • Pumpkin: a heavy gourd, the vine cut and the weight lifted.
  • Sunflower: a tall flower, its stem snipped clean.
  • Apple tree: a fruit tree, a shake of leaves and apples dropping into the grass.
  • Mushroom: mushrooms on a damp log, a soft pop as each comes away.

Around the crops

  • 21 field tool sounds: hoeing, cutting grass, chopping and felling a tree, breaking stone, digging, filling the watering can, a seed bag, fertilising and setting fence posts.
  • 13 kitchen sounds: chopping, stirring, a pan sizzle and a pot simmer (both loops), the oven, plates, a timer and a pour.
  • 13 home and shop sounds: the hearth fire, crickets at night and rain on the greenhouse (all loops), the shop bell, the shipping bin, the mailbox, going to bed and waking up, a crate, and a harvest basket filling: a few, half and full, each longer than the last (2 measured steps, each at least 12% longer, failing steps: 0).
  • 12 soft interface sounds: menus, selects, confirm and cancel, picking up and placing items, a notification and tasks.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by crop and stage.
  • 5 seamless loops of 4 seconds with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 21 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness, so the tenth hoe stroke of the morning is not the first one again.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.89 dB, so a falling tree and a menu tick share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 979 checks, 0 failed.

Honest limits

These are synthesised, stylised sounds designed for games, not field recordings. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. No animals, no fishing (that lives in a separate pack), no coins and nothing musical: a crop ripening is a soft sparkle, never a jingle.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Slackwater, fishing: the cast, the bite, the fight and the water you fish, for the pond beside the farm.
  • Longhaul, survival, gathering and the camp at night.
  • Alembic, the alchemist's workbench: brewing what you grow.
